- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to over-forecast (especially after spikes), so reduce forecasted peaks by 5–15%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a downward correction of 3–8% for the immediate follow-up period.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model may lag in adjusting downward; anticipate mean reversion and adjust forecast mid-period.
- Model underestimates true price when sentiment is positive and recent history shows volatility; increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often over-predicts early in the forecast window; apply a 2–5% downward bias to first 7–10 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction, not historical mean.
